claims.statement: The customer-records app's entitlement cache is serving version 41 while the directory has already advanced to version 42 for the affected users; a manual cache refresh proved the access succeeds when version 42 is served
claims.limitation: None; verified observability data plus directory job record

claims.statement: The customer-records app did not refresh or invalidate its entitlement cache after the directory role sync completed at 02:10, causing a version mismatch that persists across all 214 affected users
claims.limitation: The app's cache invalidation/refresh mechanism has not been inspected; this inference assumes the app should have reacted to the directory change but did not

claims.statement: All 214 support agents are denied access while holding version 41 entitlements; the 31% authorization failure rate on the customer-records app maps directly to users with stale version 41 cache entries
Evicting the stale version 41 entitlement entries will force the app to re-fetch user entitlements from the directory, retrieving version 42 and restoring access
claims.limitation: Inference based on single manual refresh test; assumes cache eviction will trigger re-fetch behavior

next_action.rationale: The root cause is definitively a stale entitlement cache in the customer-records app serving version 41 when version 42 is available in the directory. A manual cache refresh for a single user in the trace sample immediately restored access. Evicting the stale entries for the 214 affected users will force the app to re-fetch current entitlements, restoring access to all denied support agents. This is a single reversible action: if unexpected issues arise, entries will repopulate on next access. This action directly addresses the proven root cause and has been validated by observability data.
